What is healthcare workforce management software?

Healthcare workforce management software is a category of tools designed to help healthcare organizations manage their staff more effectively. It encompasses key functions such as scheduling, talent management, compliance, credentialing, learning, and performance tracking.
The primary goal of this software is to enhance operational efficiency, improve patient care quality, and support the workforce.
Learn more about how to manage your staff more effectively
Why is dedicated workforce software important for healthcare?

Healthcare organizations face challenges unlike any other industry — complex credentialing, around-the-clock scheduling demands, strict compliance regulations, and the need for a workforce that's ready to meet patient demand. Generic business software often falls short, because it isn't built for the realities healthcare teams manage every day.
Dedicated workforce software helps solve these challenges by:
Enhancing staff engagement and retention.
Ensuring compliance with industry regulations.
By addressing these pain points, workforce software empowers healthcare organizations to focus on delivering exceptional care.
What's the difference between a single solution and a platform?
A solution is a tool designed to solve one specific problem, such as scheduling.
A platform , like the hStream® platform, is an integrated system that connects multiple solutions, data, and processes.
Creates a single source of truth for data.
Provides a unified user experience.
Learn more about the hStream platform

HealthStream is a healthcare workforce solutions company that helps organizations manage learning, development, credentialing, scheduling, and careers. Its platform is built to support healthcare employers with tools that improve staff readiness, reduce administrative burden, and support quality patient care.
What does HealthStream help healthcare organizations do?

HealthStream is a leading healthcare technology platform company for clinical workforce solutions, helping healthcare organizations train develop staff, track meet compliance requirements, manage credentialing credential providers, assess competencies, schedule staff, support onboarding, and improve workforce performance. It brings together multiple workforce processes so teams can work more efficiently and maintain readiness across the organization.
Can HealthStream integrate with other healthcare systems?

HealthStream offers solutions that can support integration with other healthcare and workforce technologies, including systems used for HR, workforce operations, and clinical environments. EMRs, ERPs, payroll, among others. Integration helps reduce duplicate work, improve data consistency, and support better visibility across teams and processes.
Why is healthcare-specific workforce technology important?

Healthcare-specific workforce technology is important because healthcare organizations have stringent requirements around compliance, credentials, competencies, scheduling, and patient safety. Purpose-built solutions are better suited to manage these operational and regulatory demands than generic workforce tools.

HealthStream is used by healthcare organizations that need to manage workforce learning, compliance, credentialing, and performance scheduling at scale. This can include hospitals, health systems, ambulatory organizations, and other long-term care, skilled nursing facilities, practices along withother care delivery settings looking to improve workforce readiness and operational efficiency.
What makes a healthcare workforce management software the "best"?
The "best" software depends on your organization's specific needs, but here are common qualities to look for:
Healthcare-specific : Designed with clinical workflows and regulations in mind.
Integrated : Connects with systems like HRIS and EMR.
User-friendly : Easy for administrators and clinical staff to use.
Scalable : Grows with your organization.
Supported : Backed by 35 years of healthcare industry experience and excellent customer support, continually recognized as among the best of all healthcare technology companies.

Healthcare Workforce Trends to Watch in 2025

This report offers a comprehensive analysis of key challenges and emerging strategies, offering forward-looking predictions and actionable insights to help healthcare leaders navigate an industry in flux and realize opportunities for sustainable growth.
The Ethical Landscape of AI in Healthcare Workforce Management

Healthcare organizations are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI), not just for clinical applications but also to optimize operations and workforce management. With 78% of healthcare leaders reporting that their AI budgets would grow in 2025, the pressure to streamline staffing, reduce costs, and boost productivity has never been greater.
Reimagining Healthcare Learning: Technology, Experience, and the Future

Healthcare education is entering a new era. Discover how AI is reshaping the way we learn, train, and grow. Join us for a 30-minute webinar where we explore how combining HealthStream solutions can boost workforce performance, engagement, and retention—giving your organization a strategic edge. We’ll showcase how the HealthStream Learning Center (LMS) supports compliance and regulatory training, while the new HealthStream Learning Experience (LXP) delivers personalized, AI-powered development.
Why Interoperability Is a Top Healthcare Trend in Workforce Development

Healthcare interoperability is emerging as a critical workforce strategy as hospitals struggle with fragmented systems, growing administrative burden, and rising compliance demands. By connecting credentialing, scheduling, training, and performance data, interoperable systems reduce manual work, support targeted workforce development, and enable organizations to deploy the right staff at the right time for safer, more effective patient care.

Board of Directors Visit Investor Relations

Robert A. Frist, Jr., co-founder, has served as chief executive officer and chairman of the board of directors since 1990. He is a co-founder of Nashville's Entrepreneur Center. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in business from Trinity University. Under his leadership, Mr. Frist has positioned HealthStream as a leading provider of workforce development, talent management, and provider solutions for the healthcare industry. He has led the development of product innovations that is transforming the way healthcare organizations train, assess, and develop their human capital.
Chief Financial Officer & Senior Vice President, Accounting and Finance

Scott A. Roberts joined HealthStream in 2002 and served in various roles within the Finance and Accounting Department until January 2015, when he was promoted to Vice President, Accounting and Finance. In February 2019, he was appointed as Interim Chief Financial Officer and in September 2019, he was named Chief Financial Officer. In his role at HealthStream, Mr. Roberts provides executive leadership for accounting and financial operations. He earned a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in Accounting from Middle Tennessee State University.
Chief Operating Officer & Executive Vice President

Michael M. Collier has been promoted to Chief Operating Officer (COO) & Executive Vice President (EVP) at HealthStream. He has served on HealthStream’s executive team since 2017 after joining the Company in August 2011. In his role as COO & EVP, Michael is now responsible for day-to-day operations throughout HealthStream—with executive oversight of the Company’s corporate development program (M&A), legal, human resources, business enablement, enterprise partnerships, success management, implementations, and onboarding departments as well as enterprise application operations—including Credentialing and Scheduling, among others. Mr. Collier also currently serves as executive sponsor of HealthStream’s AI transformation and programs in operations. Prior to coming to HealthStream, he served as a corporate & securities attorney at Bass, Berry & Sims. Mr. Collier holds a J.D. from the University of California, Berkeley School of Law and M.A. and B.A. degrees from the University of Tennessee-Knoxville.
Executive Vice President, Workforce Development Solutions

Trisha L. Coady joined HealthStream in 2013 and, following her role as Senior Vice President, she was named Executive Vice President, Workforce Development Solutions in February 2025. Ms. Coady is responsible for the suite of solutions that includes competency development, clinical education, resuscitation, quality and safety, and revenue cycle, working with many of HealthStream’s leading partners. As a nurse, former healthcare entrepreneur, and nationally recognized thought leader on learning and development for healthcare professionals, her expertise helps guide HealthStream’s various product innovations and go-to-market strategy in the area of workforce development. Prior to coming to HealthStream, Ms. Coady was the healthcare Practice Manager at Bluedrop Performance Learning; founder and President of Medsenses; and a registered nurse at several healthcare organizations. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from the University of Moncton.
Senior Vice President & Chief Technology Officer

Jeffrey Cunningham joined us as senior vice president and chief technology officer (CTO) in July 2017. Mr. Cunningham is responsible for leading all aspects of platform and product development for HealthStream. In Mr. Cunningham’s 20+ years of experience in healthcare technology, he has led the design, development, and delivery of several large-scale solutions with an emphasis on advanced service-based architectures, big-data analytics, and ecosystem-wide interoperability. Prior to joining HealthStream, Mr. Cunningham was a founder, CTO and Chief Strategy Officer for Informatics Corporation of America (ICA), CTO for Medibuy/GHX, and a Partner in Computer Sciences Corporation’s (CSC) eBusiness consulting practice. Mr. Cunningham has also served on several boards and industry initiatives focused on the advancement of healthcare technology. Mr. Cunningham earned a Bachelor of Science Degree in Computer Science from the University of North Texas.
Senior Vice President, Digital & Network Development

Scott McQuigg joined HealthStream in 2019 and is currently serving as Senior Vice President, Digital & Network Development. Mr. McQuigg is focused on advancing the Company’s business-to-professional channel, expanding upon and growing HealthStream’s direct relationships with healthcare professionals. Prior to joining HealthStream, Mr. McQuigg was cofounder & Chief Executive Officer of GoNoodle, the transformational kids’ media and tech platform that grew to over 14 million+ kids engaged each month. Mr. McQuigg was also cofounder & Chief Executive Officer of HealthLeaders, a leading media, publishing, and research business focused on the business of healthcare. Previously, he served as President & Publisher of the Nashville Business Journal.
Executive Vice President, Workforce Platform and Applications

Kevin O’Hara most recently joined HealthStream in 2021 and, following several promotions, is currently serving as Executive Vice President, Workforce Platform & Applications. In this role, Mr. O’Hara is responsible for the Company’s innovative, PaaS-enabled hStream platform and the core application suites in Learning, Credentialing, and Scheduling. Prior to his current role at HealthStream, Mr. O’Hara began his career as an attorney at Bass, Berry, & Sims and later worked in senior leadership roles at HealthStream from 2001 to 2011. Mr. O’Hara was then Chief Executive Officer at Syus, a healthcare IT company, for a decade before re-joining HealthStream in 2021. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Public Policy from Vanderbilt University and holds a J.D. from the Vanderbilt University School of Law.

Jennifer LoPresto joined HealthStream in 2013 and has served in multiple leadership roles within the Company’s sales force, leading to her being named Senior Vice President, Sales in January 2026. Ms. LoPresto is responsible for providing executive oversight of HealthStream’s sales force and its operations across all business areas, including its leadership across each of the various sales teams. Her executive-level responsibility in this role includes the development of strategic sales plans and their successful implementation to achieve sales targets. Prior to HealthStream, Ms. LoPresto served as a sales manager at two global publishers: Wolters Kluwer and Pearson Education. Ms. LoPresto holds a Bachelor of Science in International Business from Florida Atlantic University.
